meta.titre: Extract precise figures from a reading passage to answer a comprehension question

sections.contenu_markdown: When a comprehension question asks for a specific number, a date, or a quantity, there is no room for approximation - unlike a "why" question, which allows some rephrasing, a figures question has only one exactly correct answer.

items: Careful scanning of a passage for numbers and quantities
Distinguishing between similar figures that might appear close together in a passage

sections.titre: Extracting exact figures from a passage
sections.contenu_markdown:
When a question asks for a specific figure (a number, a date, a quantity, a score), the answer must be copied EXACTLY as it appears in the passage - unlike other comprehension questions, there is no need (and no benefit) to paraphrase a number.

Special attention must be paid when a passage contains several similar or related figures close together (for example, a "before" and "after" value): the question usually asks for one specific figure, or for the relationship between two (such as an improvement, a difference, or a total), and confusing which figure corresponds to which moment or category is the most common source of error.
sections.formule_principale: \text{Figures question} \Rightarrow \text{copy the exact number/date from the passage, never approximate}

sections.enonce_markdown: Passage extract: "In 2020, the school had only 3 computers for over 400 students. By 2024, thanks to a donation, this number had risen to 25." Question: How many computers did the school have in 2024?

etapes.action: Locate all the figures mentioned in the relevant passage
etapes.justification: The passage contains several numbers (3, 400, 2020, 25, 2024) that must not be confused.

etapes.action: Match each figure to what it represents and when
etapes.justification: The question specifically asks about the year 2024, not 2020.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 2024 corresponds to 25 computers, not 3 (which was the 2020 figure)

etapes.justification: Only the figure matching the exact year asked should be given.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The correct answer is 25 (not 3, which was the earlier 2020 figure, and not 400, which refers to the number of students, not computers): careful matching of each figure to its correct year and category avoids this common confusion.

items.erreur_markdown: Confusing two similar figures that appear close together in the passage (e.g. giving the "before" figure when the "after" figure was requested).
items.pourquoi_faux: Passages often deliberately present a contrast between two related figures (before/after, old/new) precisely to test careful reading; picking the wrong one shows insufficiently careful attention to which moment or category the question specifically asks about.
items.correction_markdown: Always re-read the exact wording of the question (which year? which category?) before writing down a figure, to make sure the right one is selected.

items.erreur_markdown: Rounding or approximating a figure instead of copying it exactly as written in the passage.
items.pourquoi_faux: Unlike a general comprehension answer, a figure has one single, precise correct value; rounding it (for example writing "about 25" instead of the passage's exact figure) is treated as an inaccurate answer.
items.correction_markdown: Always copy figures exactly as they appear in the passage, without rounding, approximating, or converting units unless specifically asked to.

items.enonce_markdown: Passage extract: "The clinic treated 120 patients in January and 150 in February." Question: How many patients did the clinic treat in February?
Passage extract: "Tickets cost 500 francs for adults and 250 francs for children under twelve." Question: How much does a ticket cost for a 10-year-old child?
items.solution_markdown: 250 francs — a 10-year-old is under twelve, so the child price applies, not the adult price of 500 francs.

items.enonce_markdown: Passage extract: "The number of students enrolled rose from 800 in 2018 to 1,200 in 2023 - an increase the headmaster described as remarkable." A question asks for the INCREASE in enrolment, not simply the final figure. Give the correct answer and explain the calculation.
items.solution_markdown: The increase in enrolment is 1,200 − 800 = 400 students. This question specifically asks for the DIFFERENCE between the two figures (the increase), not simply the final enrolment figure (1,200) nor the initial one (800) taken alone: giving only one of these two figures, without calculating the actual increase between them, would not fully answer what was asked.

items_markdown: A figures question requires the exact number/date as it appears in the passage, never an approximation.
When several similar figures appear close together, carefully match each one to its correct year/category before answering.
Re-read the exact wording of the question (which year? which group?) before selecting a figure.
If a question asks for a DIFFERENCE or INCREASE between two figures, calculate it rather than giving just one of the two values.
